canObsR is installed in two commands: one installs the R package, the other (`canobs_setup()`) installs
everything canObsR needs outside R. This page explains both, what they print, and what to do if something goes
wrong. It is the same on Windows, macOS and Linux, and **no administrator rights are needed**.

## What is installed, and why

canObsR is a thin R package. The processing itself (Time-SIFT, colour calibration, co-registration) is done by
**canobspy**, a Python package shipped inside canObsR, with two Python libraries that have no R equivalent:
**GDAL** (Python bindings) and **AROSICS** (co-registration of images). Python runs in a dedicated **conda
environment**, called `canobs`, and always in a separate process: it never interferes with the GDAL of the R
packages `terra` and `sf`, nor with other Python installations of your computer.

| Component | Needed for | Installed by |
|---|---|---|
| R package canObsR | everything | `remotes::install_github()` |
| conda (Miniforge if you have none) | the Python environment | `canobs_setup()` |
| environment `canobs`: Python 3.12, GDAL, AROSICS, canobspy | everything | `canobs_setup()` |
| [OpenDroneMap](https://opendronemap.org) (ODM) | `generate_Mosa(engine = "odm")`, the default | you (installer), detected by `canobs_setup()` |
| Agisoft Metashape Professional (2.x licence) | `generate_Mosa(engine = "metashape")` | you (application), `canobs_install_metashape()` (Python module), optional |
| NVIDIA GPU | ODM 3 to 4 times faster | optional |

Disk space: about 3 GB for the conda environment (plus ~0.5 GB for Miniforge if it is installed), 6 GB for ODM.

## 1. Install R (and RStudio)

R 4.0 or later ([CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/)); RStudio is recommended but not required.
Rtools is **not** needed: canObsR contains no code to compile.

## 2. Install the R package

```{r}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("umr-amap/canObsR")
```

> During the development of version 1.0, use the development branch instead:
> `remotes::install_github("PPierre22/canObsR@v1-restructure")`

## 3. Install the Python environment: `canobs_setup()`

In a **new R session** (RStudio: *Session > Restart R*):

```{r}
canObsR::canobs_setup()
```

The first run takes **5 to 15 minutes**, mostly to download the Python packages (~0.5 GB, once). They are
installed from a list of exact versions tested for each system (Windows, macOS Intel and Apple Silicon, Linux):
conda has nothing to resolve, and everybody gets the same environment. It goes
through six steps, and reports each check as `[OK]`, `[--]` (optional component not found) or `[!!]` (problem,
followed by what to do), and ends with a summary of what is still to do:

```

    log: C:/Users/me/AppData/Roaming/R/config/R/canObsR/setup_20261125_101500.log
```

What `canobs_setup()` does, and does not do:

* **conda**: it uses the conda already installed on the computer (Anaconda, Miniconda, Miniforge), or installs
  [Miniforge](https://conda-forge.org/download/) in your user folder after asking. `canobs_setup(conda = "miniforge")`
  always uses a Miniforge of its own, whatever else is installed: the safest choice when the existing conda is old
  or behaves strangely.
* **environment**: packages come from **conda-forge only**. An existing environment of another name is never
  modified; `canobs` is created once, then only checked.
* **configuration**: saved in your user folder; the next R sessions find the environment, ODM, etc.
  automatically. Nothing is added to your `PATH`, nothing is written in `.Rprofile`.
* It can be run again at any time: what is installed is only checked. **Run it again after each update of
  canObsR** (it updates canobspy) **and after installing or updating ODM** (it detects it and checks its GPU).

## 4. Install OpenDroneMap (default photogrammetry engine)

* **Windows**: `canobs_setup()` offers to install it; otherwise, at any time:

  ```{r}
  canObsR::canobs_install_odm()
  ```

  It downloads the installer of the version of ODM used to test canObsR (3.6.2, 245 MB), installs it in `C:/ODM`
  without administrator rights (Windows may ask permission to install the Microsoft Visual C++ libraries: accept),
  records it in the configuration and checks the GPU. To install it by hand: `ODM_Setup_x.y.z.exe` from
  <https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/ODM/releases>, then `canobs_setup()` again (or
  `canobs_setup(odm_path = "D:/ODM/run.bat")` if it is not in `C:/ODM`).
* **Linux / macOS**: ODM runs with [docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)
  (`generate_Mosa(..., odm_runner = "docker")`), or natively on Linux (`odm_path = ".../run.sh"`).

**NVIDIA GPU (Windows)**: the Windows installer of ODM contains a dummy `nvcuda.dll` that hides the NVIDIA driver,
so ODM silently computes on the processor (3 to 4 times slower). `canobs_setup()` and `generate_Mosa()` detect
it and rename it `nvcuda.dll.odm_dummy`; if they cannot (no write access to the ODM folder), they print a warning
that cannot be missed: rename it yourself, once, as administrator. Without an NVIDIA GPU, nothing to do.

## 5. Metashape (optional)

To use `generate_Mosa(engine = "metashape")`, you need Metashape Professional with a **2.x licence activated on
the computer** (in the application: *Help > Activate product*), and its Python module in the environment of
canObsR:

```{r}
canObsR::canobs_install_metashape()
```

It downloads the Python module of Metashape (2.3.2 by default, ~150 MB), installs it and checks that the licence
is activated. A 2.x licence works with every 2.x version: the module can be more recent than the application.
Modules before 2.3 cannot be used on Windows (they do not support the Python 3.12 of canObsR). Without internet
access to agisoft.com: download the *Python 3 Module* from <https://www.agisoft.com/downloads/installer/>, then
`canobs_install_metashape(wheel = "<path of the .whl file>")`.

## 6. Check the installation

```{r}
canObsR::canobs_sitrep()
```

prints what is installed and checks that it still works (it installs nothing). **Copy its output, and the log
file it names, in any bug report** (<https://github.com/umr-amap/canObsR/issues>).

A first real test, on a folder of drone images (one subfolder per date, e.g. `RGB_20250101`):

```{r}
chk <- canObsR::check_flights("D:/my_data/rawData")   # reads the EXIF of the images, changes nothing
chk$folders
```

## Troubleshooting

| Message | Cause, and what to do |
|---|---|
| `download of Miniforge failed` | No internet access, proxy or firewall. Behind a proxy, set it before: `Sys.setenv(https_proxy = "http://proxy:port", http_proxy = "http://proxy:port")`. Or install Miniforge by hand (<https://conda-forge.org/download/>, "Just Me") and run `canobs_setup(conda = "<folder>/Scripts/conda.exe")`. |
| `conda could not create the environment` | Look at the last lines printed, the full output is in the log. Frequent causes: proxy (conda needs `https://conda.anaconda.org`), antivirus blocking files, disk full, old conda. Try `canobs_setup(conda = "miniforge")`. |
| `the path of conda contains spaces or accents` | Some packages fail to install there (frequent with Windows user names). `canobs_setup(conda = "miniforge")` installs Miniforge in `C:/canobs-miniforge3` in that case. |
| `The Python environment of canObsR is not installed` | `canobs_setup()` has not been run on this computer, or the environment was deleted: run it. |
| `canobspy x differs from canObsR y` | canObsR was updated: run `canobs_setup()`. |
| `ODM WILL NOT USE THE GPU` | See *NVIDIA GPU* above. |
| Anything else | `canobs_setup(reinstall = TRUE)` recreates the environment from scratch. Otherwise, open an issue with the output of `canobs_sitrep()` and the log. |

## Uninstall

```{r}
cfg <- canObsR::canobs_config()
cfg$envdir                                   # the conda environment: delete this folder
tools::R_user_dir("canObsR", "config")       # configuration and logs: delete this folder
remove.packages("canObsR")
```

Miniforge, if `canobs_setup()` installed it, is in `%LOCALAPPDATA%/canobs/miniforge3` (Windows) or
`~/.local/share/canobs/miniforge3`: delete that folder too.
